senses.gloss: --Nikumbha appeared in the disguise of a barber of this name in a dream to दिवोदास before the ruin of the city and asked him to find his abode in the outskirts of the kingdom. वा. ९२. ३८. [page२-593+ २४]
(I)--the Matsya king, slain by परशुराम. Br. III. ३८. ४९, ५१.
(II)--a commander of भण्ड, vanquished by स्वप्नेशी. Br. IV. २१. ८५; २८. ४१.
(I)--a servant maid of पार्वती. Br. IV. ४०. २५.
(II)--a goddess enshrined at गन्गा; a mother goddess. M. १३. ३५; १७९. २१.
--a Mt. in भारतवर्ष. भा. V. १९. १६.
--done by women to भण्ड's sons march- ing against ललिता's host. Br. IV. २६. ६२.
--a वर्ण s4akti. Br. IV. ४४. ५९.
--a R. of the भद्रा country. वा. ४३. २८.
(I)--the eleventh organ partaking of the character of कर्म and ज्ञान; proceeds to create induced by a desire to produce. Br. II. 9. 1, 7; IV. 3. २२; M. 3. २१.
(III)--a साध्य god. Br. III. 3. १६; वा. ६६. १५.
(IV)--a तुषित god. Br. III. 3. १९; वा. ६६. १८.
(V)--a शाला adjoining Sahasrastambha शाला in श्रीपुरम्; reputed for its अमृतवापिक; by drinking its water yogis and siddhas became strong in body. Br. IV. ३५. 2-२४.
(VI)--a son of शतरूपा. M. 4. २५.
(VII)--twenty-sixth kalpa; शङ्करी became twins. वा. २१. ५९.
(VIII)--another term for महान्. वा. १०२. २१.
--twelve sons of ब्रह्मा with मन्त्रशरीरस्। वा. ६७. 6. [page२-617+ २३]
--the lake of the south. वा. ३६. १६.
(I)--a Mt. of पुष्करद्वीप; the limit of पृथु's dominion; west of the city of वसवी. Br. II. १९. ११२-14, ११७; M. १२३. १६; वा. ४९. १०८; Vi. II. 8. 7-8.
(II)--a son of वपुष्मान् and the founder of the मानस kingdom. Br. II. १४. ३२, ३४; वा. ३३. २८, ३०; Vi. II. 4, २३, २९. [page२-685+ ४१]
(III)--a वम्शवर्तिन् god. Br. II. ३६. २९.
(IV)--a यक्ष; a son of देवजनी and मणि- vara. Br. III. 7. १३०.
(VI)--Father of रिष्यन्त, belonging to the commencement of the द्वापर in the ११थ् Manvantara. वा. ७०. ३०.

--the world above ब्रह्माण्ड where live the Somapa पितृस्;
1: M. १५. २५.
the country of पितृस्--सुकालस्.
2: Br. III. १०. ९७; वा. ७३. ४७.
--a Bhavya deva. Br. II. ३६. ७१.
(I)--a son of प्राचीत्वत. M. ४९. 2.
(II)--a son of Aviddha. वा. ९९. १२१.
(III)--a son of महान्त. Vi. II. 1. ३९.
(IV)--a son of प्रवीर; father of Abhayada. Vi. IV. १९. 1.
(I)--R. from lake Varcovan. (सायन- वा। प्।). Br. II. १८. ६६; वा. ४७. ६३.
(III)--the wife of मृकण्डु and mother of मार्कण्डेय. वा. २८. 5; Br. II. ११. 7. [page२-618+ २८]
(II)--a daughter of उत्तानपाद and the wife of अन्तिनार. Br. II. ३६. ९०; M. ४९. 7; वा. ६२. ७६.
(I)--a son of धिषणा and कृशाश्य. भा. VI. 6. २०.
(II)--a Pravara. M. १९६. ३०.
(III)--a साध्य god. M. २०३. ११.
(IV)--the author of a धर्मशास्त्र; grass cut for cow is not punishable; so also flowers plucked from gardens other than those of temples for the worship of god. M. २२७. २७, ३२, ११३.
(V)--approached by वरूत्रि's sons to ruin the offerings to Gods but interrupted by Indra. वा. ६५. ७९.
(VI)--a son of बाष्कल. वा. ६७. ७९.
(VII)--a son of शिघ्रक; established himself in कलापग्राम by yoga. वा. ८८. २१०.
(VIII)--one of the sons of Madhu. वा. ९५. ४५.

(IX) (रैवत)--the fifth Manu; son of Priya- vrata and brother of तामस; Bali and others were his sons. Vibhu was Indra; भूतरयस् were the gods of the epoch; वैकुण्ठ was the manifestation of Hari in this मन्वन्तर।
1: भा. V. 1. २८; VIII. 5. 2-5.
देवबाहु and others were the seven sages; served as calf to milk the earth.
2: Br. II. ३६. 3, ५१. ६४; ३७. १७. 8.
[page२-619+ ४३]
(X)--(चाक्षुष)--a son of विश्वकर्मन् (विश्- वेश-म्। प्।) and कृती। Father of विश्वस् and साध्यस्. भा. VI. 6. १५; M. १७१. ४८.

(XI) (सावर्णि)--the eighth Manu. A son of छाया and विवस्वान्. Father of Nirmoka and other sons. In this epoch Sutapas, Virajas अमिताभस्, Mukhyas were the gods. Bali was Indra. गालव, कृप, राम and others were the sages. Hari manifested himself as सार्वभौम।
1: भा. VI. 6. ४१; VIII. १३. ११-7; २२. ३१; Vi. III. 2. 4; १३-19.
Ini- tiated in the mystery of Lord's glories by नारद, worship- ping नरनारायण;
2: भा. V. १९. १०.
originally श्रुतश्रवस्; performs aus- terities on the slopes of Meru even to-day.
3: Br. IV. 1. २८; III. ५९. ४९ and ८०.

(XII) (स्वायम्भुव)--the first son of ब्रह्मा and the first king (सम्राट्) also विराट्. Ruled the earth, girt by seven seas, occupying ब्रह्मावर्त with बर्हिष्मती as capital. A विप्रराजऋषि. Learnt the Veda from his father, who asked him to rule according to Dharma. Wife शत- रूपा; sons Priyavrata and उत्तानपाद besides eight more through अनन्ता and a daughter, देवहूती. Other daughters were आकूति and प्रसूति
1: भा. VIII. 1. 1, 5 and 7, XI. १४. 4; III. २०. 1 and १०; २१. 1-3, २५-26; २२. २६-9; VI. 1. 1; 8. 6; Br. II. १३. १०५; M. 3. ४४-5; 4. ३४; १४५, ९०; वा. 3. 2, ३६; २३. ४७; ५९. ५६-7; Vi. I. 7. १४-19; III. 1. 6.
who married दक्ष and Ruci res- pectively. Met Kardama on the सरस्वती, spoke of inter- dependence of the क्षत्रिय and the Brahmana, and offered his daughter देवहूती in marriage to that sage.
2: भा. III. २१. ४५; २२. 3-१४.
Another daughter धन्या became the wife of Dhruva. Seeing Dhruva fighting with the यक्षस् in utter wrath, Manu asked him to cease slaughtering the innocents and to ask pardon of Kubera, their chief.
3: Ib. IV. ११. 6-३४; M. 4. ३८.
Appointed Priyavrata in charge of the kingdom and retired to तपस्। Spent ७१ yugas meditating on विष्णु, and gave Him the name, Hari. Did not take objection to Hara's violation of धर्म, though he was one of the twelve who knew the धर्म ordained by Hari.
4: भा. V. 1. २१-2; XI. 2. १५; III. २२. ३१-6; II. 7. 2; VI. १७. १२; 3. २०; IV. २१. २८.
Served as calf for पृथु to milk the earth.
5: Ib. IV. १८. १२; २९. ४२.
Formed one half of the Creator [page२-620+ ३८] and the other was शतरूपा. Asked ब्रह्मा for the earth being lifted out of the waters to form an abode for him and his subjects, when a वराह issued from ब्रह्मा's nostrils to do the work.
6: Ib. III. १२. ५३-4; १३. 3-१८.
Renouncing the world, Manu stood on one leg medi- tating on the glory of Hari on the bank of the सुनन्दा for a hundred years; when the Asuras tried to attack and devour him, Hari in the form of यज्ञ slew them.
7: भा. VIII. 1. 7-१०.
The first to give out स्मार्त धर्म, वर्णाश्रम धर्म and the first to practice शिष्टाचार; requested by Brahma to protect the वेदस् and consequently the यज्ञस्। Divided the Vedas into four sections.
8: Br. II. २९. ४६, ६१-4; ३०. ३४; ३२. ३५-8, ९६; ३४. 2-8; ३५. १७५; ३६. 3; ३७. १४; IV. 1. ३२ and १०९; M. १४२. ४२.
An आदिपुरुष. From him were born वैराजस्.
9: Ib. 3. ४५-6; १७१. २७; १९२. १०; २२७. ३२.

(XIII)--(स्वारोचिष)--the second Manu, and son of Agni. Father of Dyumat and others. In this epoch Rocana was Indra, तुषित and others were gods, ऊर्ज्जस्तम्ब and six others were the seven sages. भा. VIII. 1. १९-20; Br. II. ३६. 3, २३; ३७. १५.

(XV) (दक्ष सावर्णी)--the ninth Manu. Born of वरुण; father of भूतकेतु and other sons. पारस् and others were gods of his epoch, and Adbhuta was Indra; Dyu- timat and others were sages. During this period Hari mani- fested himself as ऋषभ. भा. VIII. १३. १८-20. [page२-622+ ३५]

(XVI) (रुद्रसावर्णि)--the twelfth Manu; father of देववान् and other sons. ऋतधामन् was Indra. हारित and others were gods. तपोमूर्ति and others were sages. स्वधाम was Hari manifesting in this epoch;
1: भा. VIII. १३. २७-29.
the fourth सावर्ण Manu in the १२थ् पर्याय।
2: Br. IV. 1. ८२-93.

(XVII) सावर्ण(इ)--the second Manu in the epoch of the Vaivasvata Manvantara; son of सावर्ण;
1: Br. IV. 1. ५१-5, ७३-81.
in his age Bali was to reign over the whole world.
2: Ib. II. ३६. 4; III. ७३. ५२.
(XVIII) (रौच्य)--a सावर्ण Manu of the XIII पर्याय; three groups of gods, all addicted to Soma and ghee through यज्ञस्। Br. IV. 1. ९५-116.

(XIX)--(चाक्षुषान्तरम्)--भृगु and other sages lived in this epoch.
1: M. 2. १४; 6. 3; 8. १२.
There were five classes of devas, Lekha, ऋभव, ऋभाद्य, वारिमूल, and Divaukasa; चाक्- षुष had ten sons commencing with Ruru;
2: Ib. 9. २२, २५.
King पुरूरवस् flourished in the same line in this epoch.
3: Ib. ११५. 7-8.

(XX) (औत्तम)--the third Manu;
1: M. 3. ४७.
father of ten sons; the devas of the epoch are भावनस् and there were also seven sages, कौकुरुण्डि, etc., all engaged in yoga.
2: Ib. 9. ११.
(XXI) (चाक्षुष) (VI)--the son of चक्षु and वीरिणी; married a royal princess नड्वला and had ten sons. M. 4. ४०; Vi. I. १३. 4.
(XXII)--the son of हर्यश्व and father of Pra- tika. Vi. IV. 5. २७. [page२-623+ २९]

--worshipped with Devas for kingdom; their duties in different epochs described.
1: भा. II. 3. 9; VIII. १४. 2-१०
Fourteen in number; went to Maharloka when their duties were over;
2: Br. IV. 2. 2 nad 5.
in order: स्वायम्भुव, स्वारोचिष, Auttama, तामस, Raivata, चाक्- षुष; these six are past ones; the future are eight; सावर्ण, पञ्चरौच्यस्, Bhautya and Vaivasvata.
3: वा. ६२. 3-4.
--the whole period of the fourteen Manus covering a कल्प of one thousand yugas--the fourteen man- vantaras. भा. VIII. १३. ३६; १४. ११.
--a son of द्युतिमान् after whose name is a Janapada. वा. ३३. २१.
--a तीर्थ visited by बलराम. भा. X. ७९. २१.
(मनुत्त or मरुत्त)--a king equal to a cakravartin, went to heaven with Samvarta, a sage; father of नरिष्यन्त. वा. ८६. 9.
--a daughter of Tumburu. Br. III. 7. १३.
--an अवतार् of Hari. भा. II. 7. २०. [page२-624+ २३]
--a son of Madhu. वा. ९५. ४५.

--created out of the रजस् element;
1: Vi. I. 5. २३, ३७-8; 6. 1.
four वर्णस् of.
2: Ib. I. 6. 5.
--are Laukikas (s.v.). Br. II. २८. ७१, ७८, ९५.
(I)--a son of मेधातिथि of शाकद्वीप. भा. V. २०. २५.
(II)--a son of ईशान and शिवा. Br. II. १०. ७९; वा. २७. ५२.
(III)--a Lekha god. Br. II. ३६. ७५.
(IV)--the Indra of the चाक्षुष epoch. Br. II. ३६. ७६; Vi. III. 1. २६.
(V)--a son of Anila (Anala-म्। प्।) a Vasava. Br. III. 3. २६; M. 5. २५; वा. ६६. २५; Vi. I. १५. ११४.
(VI)--a god of one of the ten branches of the हरीत gan2a. Br. IV. 1. ८४; वा. १००. ८९.
--restraint of mind. वा. १७. 6.
(I)--a son of द्युतिमान् after whom the kingdom, मानोनुग took its name. Br. II. १४. २२, २४.
(II) (च्)--a region of the क्रौञ्चद्वीप adjoining the वामन hill. Br. II. १४. २४; १९. ७१; M. १२२. ८४.
(III)--a वर्ष of the hill, वामनक. वा. ४९. ६६.
--an Apsarasa. Br. III. 7. 7.
(I)--a mind-born mother. M. १७९. २६.
(II)--an Apsarasa. वा. ६९. 6.
(I)--the सभा of ब्रह्मा on the first inner- slope of Meru in which reside ईशान and Indra besides sages and seers. वा. ३४. ७२-7.
(II)--a daughter of Tumburu. वा. ६९. ४९.
--a तीर्थ on the नर्मदा sacred to पितृस्. M. १९४. 7. [page२-626+ २८]
(I)--a wife of Dhara. M. 5. २४.
(II)--the wife of Dharma, the Vasu. Vi. I. १५. ११३.
--the form of a Brahmana assumed by गणेश Nikumbha when he appeared in a dream to दिवोदास. Br. III. ६७. ४२.
--a R. from the ऋक्ष hill. Br. II. १६. ३१.
--Indra of the चाक्षुष epoch. भा. VIII. 5. 8.

--also मन्त्रिणी,
1: Br. IV. १७. २२, २७; २७, ५८; १९. ६१.
and मन्त्रिणीश्यामा; war master of ललिता; residence at कदम्बवनवाटिका;
2: Ib. IV. ३१. ८२, ८९.
helped कुमारी in vanquishing भण्ड's sons; rode on Kiri- cakra; consulted दण्डनाथा;
3: Ib. IV. २६. 2, ८३, ११३; २७. ५८.
invoked मदीरासिन्धु (s.v.).
4: Ib. IV. २८. १४, ४८, ९२, १०३.
--a branch of the Vedic literature. वा. ५८. १४.

--a branch of Vedic literature;
1: Br. II. ३१. १२; ३३. ५४; वा. ५९. १३८.
ety. of.
2: Ib. ५०. १४१; ६१. १०२.
[page२-627+ ३८]
(II)--a portion of the पूर्व samhita1. वा. ६१. ६५.
--a R. in कुशद्वीप. भा. V. २०. १५.
--a son of सत्यभामा. वा. ९६. २३८.
--a son of सत्यभामा and कृष्ण. Br. III. ७१. २४७.
--the १२ sons who came out of ब्रह्मा's face. वा. ६७. 4. [page२-628+ २८]
--a वर्ण s4akti. Br. IV. ४४. ५८.
(I)--a वानर chief. Br. III. 7. २३८.
--the ministry which ruled the king- dom in the absence of king, Sagara. Br. III. ५०. ३२.
--a secret mantra in honour of Sankar- षण, taught to king Citraketu by नारद; its text. भा. VI. १५. २७; १६. १८-25.
--a son of वीरव्रत and भोजा; his wife was सत्या, and son Bhauvana. भा. V. १५. १५.

--a son of Abhramu elephant;
1: Br. III. 7. ३३०.
also Padma; the vehicle of Kubera.
2: वा. ६९. २१४, २१६.
--a son of श्रीदेवा and Vasudeva. Br. III. ७१. १८१. [page२-629+ ३६]
--the शूद्र caste of शाकद्वीप. Vi. II. 4. ६९.
--a R. from the Suktimat hill. Br. II. १६. ३८.
--a मूर्छन; the presiding deity of the विश्- vedevas. वा. ८६. ६३.
--a Marut गण. M. १७१. ५४.
--a son of बलराम. Br. III. ७१. १६७.

(I)--(Mt.) on one side of Meru; one of विष्- kambhagiris round the Meru; sacred to शिव; in its valleys हिरण्यकशिपु performed austerities; used in churning the milk ocean; lest it should sink in the sea Hari in the form of कूर्म supported the mountain; was lifted up with great difficulty by the Gods and Asuras, who could not carry it to the ocean, when Hari asked गरुड to bear it on his back to the sea and which he did.
1: Br. IV. 9. ५१, ५६, ६०; भा. I. 3. १६; III. २८. २७; V. १६. ११; VII. 3. 2; 7. 2; VIII. 5. १०; 6. ३३-9; X. ४०. १८; XII. १३. 2; M. ६९. 1; २४९. १५; २५०. २६; २५१. ३५; Vi. I. 9. ७७, ८४.
Recipient of mango fruits as large as hill-tops falling from a divine mango tree, ११०० yoja- nas high (see अरुणोदा).
2: भा. V. १६. १६.
Here पृथु died and was cre- mated.
3: Ib. IV. २३. २४.
